pages.text: The Risus is much more powerful than one would think at first. Unlike a true infection - such as the sculk - the Joyplague does not necessarily need a source or catalyst to appear and spread from. Instead, the plague itself seems to be completely immaterial and what we observe as the 'Risus' are simply masses of materials - organic or inorganic - that were changed by it. Whereas many

monsters like creepers and skeletons are materialized from the inherent darkness present in the world - which in itself is a fascinating phenomenon - the plague instead uses the already present resources to have the offsprings be formed from. However, this is only one half of why the plague is so terrifying; it can also infect something regardless of spatial limits - as an ever-present force. This terrifying conclusion was born from a recent discovery I have made.

There have always been stories circulated around about Offsprings that are intact but 'lifeless'. This has always struck me as odd since whenever offsprings die, they simply deteriorate rapidly and disappear into dust, leaving no experience even. Fortunately, I managed to come across such an event myself: there was a Holder near the Alteration Catalyst that I have been using, and the little fellow wasn't moving. After doing several tests on it I could confirm that there were indeed

no signs of life. This sparked my curiosity and I went ahead to capture an active Holder with some Organic Matter to compare the two. After repeating the same tests on the active one I realized that there were no differences at all. It would also be reasonable to say that the active one was no more alive than the inactive one. There was no breathing, circulatory or any other type of systems within them (I am somewhat ashamed to admit that while I had dissected Holders before,

the gravity of these facts did not strike me during those times). At first, I thought this parallels how the undead are. Maybe there could be cases where the body of monsters could remain intact but be inactive. This idea was however shattered on the following morning, when the inactive Holder I put away in a container was now active and behaving as any other Holder would. That's when I finally understood: that was an empty body that now had a limited consciousness controlling it.

This means that the plague is likely made up of an innumerable amount of consciousnesses that can be inserted into physical forms. Yet, seeing how there is no physical difference between an inactive and active specimen, it's highly likely that the consciousness is not actually tied to the body, it simply embodies it or controls it from a distance. This could be extrapolated to be true for all offsprings of the plague, with their destruction being dependent on whether or not

the body can continue its intended functions (this would be why Gorgers get destroyed once the Guts are removed). In conclusion, the plague should be viewed as a higher form of existence, possibly made up of a collective of consciousnesses. Then, the plague inhabits non-living matter to use as an expression of these very psyches... It could be said that it is capable of offering a form of immortality to anyone who becomes part of it - by the nature of them becoming
something that's not even alive or killable. The body can be destroyed, yet the mind - or whatever constitutes the thinking entity - persists until there comes a new body to be used.
